---
title: "5) Annual series"
lang: en
---

The **annual** scale summarizes the series into one value per year — useful for
trends. Here it is **derived from the monthly** series (mean of the valid months
of each year).

## Code

::: {.lang-python}
```python
import tropomi_ch4 as tch4
from tropomi_ch4 import plot

df = tch4.annual(start="2019-01-01", end=None)
df.to_csv("serie_anual_ch4_brasil.csv", index=False)

plot.plot_series(df, title="Annual mean CH4 over Brazil — TROPOMI",
                 outfile="serie_anual_ch4_brasil.png")
```
:::

::: {.lang-r}
```r
source("r/tropomi_ch4.R")

anual <- ch4_anual("2019-01-01")
write.csv(anual, "serie_anual_ch4_brasil.csv", row.names = FALSE)

plot(anual$ano, anual$ch4_ppb, type = "o", pch = 20, col = "darkred",
     xlab = "Year", ylab = "CH4 (ppb)", main = "Annual CH4 over Brazil — TROPOMI")
```
:::

## What about the API's `P1Y`?

The Statistical API accepts ISO 8601 periods. `P1D` and `P1M` work reliably; the
**`P1Y` (annual) granularity needs verification** for your use case.
[requer verificação]

So the recommended path is to derive the annual from the monthly (fewer requests,
you control missing months, reproducible). If `P1Y` works in your test, just swap
the interval (`"P1Y"`).

Notebook: [`notebooks/03_anual.ipynb`](https://github.com/LudimiladeAzevedoBeltran/tropomi-ch4-brasil/blob/main/notebooks/03_anual.ipynb).
